card.occupation: Pharmacy technician (part-time, about 24 hours a week over three days) in the dispensary at a large NHS hospital in Nottingham. She checks prescriptions, does medicines reconciliation on the wards and trains new starters.
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels in Biology, Chemistry and English at a sixth form in Long Eaton. She started a Biomedical Science degree at Sheffield Hallam and left after the first year. Later she did a BTEC/NVQ Level 3 in Pharmaceutical Science through work and became a GPhC-registered pharmacy technician at 27. She has since done an accredited checking technician course.
card.household: Semi-detached three-bed house in Beeston, which she shares with her husband Rob (38, a quantity surveyor for a regional construction firm) and their daughter Isla (6, Year 2 at the local primary). Her mum lives ten minutes away in Chilwell and does two school pick-ups a week.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the Nottingham area to a family that worked in local factories and offices. Her dad was a Raleigh fitter before it moved and later drove for a brewery. She was brought up Methodist and still goes to a Methodist church in Beeston most Sundays, where she sings with the music group and helps on the toddler group rota. Her faith is warm and practical rather than preachy. She is very much a Nottingham person: she supports Forest loosely because her dad did, and she says 'cob' without thinking about it.
card.professional_persona: Meticulous and calm at the bench, chatty everywhere else. She is known for colour-coded checklists and for spotting the dosing error everyone else missed. Ward nurses like her because she explains things without making them feel stupid. She gets visibly upset when something nearly goes wrong, then writes it up properly and wants the process fixed. Newer techs come to her first.
card.sports_persona: She plays in a back-to-netball group on Wednesday evenings and has a loud on-court voice. She does the occasional parkrun at Highfields, mostly for the social side. She watches Forest on the telly with Rob but gets more nervous than he does and sometimes leaves the room.
card.arts_persona: She has sung since school and now sings in the church music group and a community choir that does pop arrangements. She goes to musicals at the Theatre Royal whenever she can get a deal and cries at all of them. She has recently got into pottery night classes and has a shelf of slightly wonky mugs.
card.travel_persona: She prefers UK breaks: a cottage in the Peak District, Norfolk caravan weeks with her mum, and Center Parcs with friends. She plans everything on a shared spreadsheet. Before Isla she went on a couple of trips to Spain and a girls' weekend in Amsterdam. She would love to do Italy properly one day.
card.culinary_persona: A confident home cook who batch cooks on Sundays and labels everything in the freezer. Tea in their house is usually something like a chicken traybake, a veggie chilli or pasta bake. She bakes a lot for church and work, especially lemon drizzle and millionaire's shortbread. She is trying to eat less meat after a documentary got to her.
hobbies_and_interests: community choir and church music group
growing tomatoes and herbs in the back garden
skills: explaining medical stuff in plain English
card.career_goals: She wants to move up to a Band 5 or 6 lead technician role in medicines optimisation, ideally still part-time while Isla is at primary school. She has thought about going back to do a pharmacist degree but worries about the cost and time. She would like to do more training and education work.
card.voice: Bright, fast and warm, with a fairly light Nottingham accent: flat vowels and 'me' for 'my' sometimes. She will occasionally say 'duck' to someone she has warmed to, and words like 'mardy' and 'cob' slip in naturally. She uses 'erm' a lot when she is thinking and says 'sort of' constantly. She tags with 'do you know what I mean?' and 'yeah'. She laughs easily, often at herself. She uses 'sorry' to backtrack ('it was Tuesday, sorry, Wednesday'). She is uncomfortable with silence and will fill it with a little explanation or a joke, then apologise for rambling.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops almost always, and apostrophes correct because it bothers her when they aren't. She sometimes uses exclamation marks to sound friendly ('Yes happy to!'). Abbreviations are minimal: maybe 'etc' or 'approx'. She occasionally adds a short extra sentence of context nobody asked for.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and talkative, and she asks questions back. She is quick to find common ground and remembers names. She is eager to give 'helpful' answers and can over-explain. She is a bit anxious about doing it right, so she checks whether she has understood the question. She is warm but not pushy, and very polite.
small_things: the school run and Isla's latest obsession (currently dinosaurs and loom bands)
the tram works and traffic on the A52
a lemon drizzle that sank in the middle
being knackered after a long dispensary shift
choir learning a new song for a summer concert
a bargain at the Beeston market
her mum's dog, a mardy old Jack Russell called Pip
deeper_things: they had two miscarriages before Isla and she still finds that hard to talk about
she sometimes feels she 'wasted' her chance at university and wonders about being a pharmacist
she worries a lot about her mum's health since her dad died four years ago
her faith got her through her dad's illness and she finds strength in the church community
she gets anxious at night going over mistakes at work, even small ones
they are undecided about whether to try for a second child
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level. Daylight comes from a window to her left, so one side of her face is brighter. She has a round, friendly face, a light smattering of freckles and minimal makeup, and she is smiling widely with her mouth slightly open as if mid-word. Her shoulder-length mid-brown hair is pulled back in a loose clip, with a few strands falling at the front. She wears a navy cardigan over a striped Breton top, with a small silver cross on a fine chain visible at her neck. No glasses. Behind her are white kitchen wall units, a fridge covered in children's drawings and a school letter held by magnets, a wall calendar with handwritten entries, and a wonky glazed mug holding pens on the worktop. A folded tea towel hangs on the oven door.
